extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark of 20,000 self-contradictory instructions across language-language and vision-language paradigms, designed to evaluate large multimodal models' ability to detect conflicting instructions.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using AutoCreate, an automatic dataset creation framework that starts from a small batch of manually input seeds and iteratively generates, decorates with contradictions, cleans, quality-checks, and expands the seed pool using programs, large language models, and human experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Experiments, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include manually input seeds, generated language and vision data from LLMs/programs, and external ImageNet data for SemanticConflict.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Generated data are deliberately modified to introduce contradictions, such as modifying image captions, changing maximum values to minimum values in charts, altering descriptive phrases to refer to non-existent objects, and substituting correct labels with similar but different objects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The unified generation process is generator-decorator-cleaner, where the cleaner removes data that does not meet quality standards, followed by quality checks by human experts and LLMs; the resulting dataset is refined to extract new seeds for the next iteration.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts manually selected the SCI-Base and SCI-Core subsets and rigorously checked dataset quality. For evaluation labels in experiments, replies were evaluated by human experts and also by GPT-4 as an evaluation agent using a uniform prompt to determine whether a reply identified the conflict.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes agreement between GPT-4 evaluation and human expert evaluation using Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate, finding close alignment.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to help assess and improve multimodal models' handling of conflicting instructions, promote inclusivity in AI research through diverse instruction datasets, enhance context-aware understanding, and improve trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Only one conflict type, SemanticConflict, uses external ImageNet data; performance differences across models may also stem from differences in training data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark currently includes only language-language and vision-language paradigms, does not provide fine-grained control over conflict degree, and does not include a detailed study of attention mechanisms under conflicting instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating large multimodal models on their ability to detect self-contradictory or conflicting instructions; facilitating qualitative evaluation via SCI-Core, SCI-Base, and SCI-All subsets.

name.evidence: Hence, we propose a multimodal benchmark, Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI), to evaluate the ability of LMMs to detect conflicted instructions

description.evidence: It encompasses 20K conflicting instructions and 8 tasks, evenly distributed between language-language and vision-language paradigms (Fig. 2).

inLanguage.evidence: Abstract. Large multimodal models (LMMs) excel in adhering to human instructions.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: SCI is constructed using our novel automatic dataset creation framework, AutoCreate (Fig. 3), which builds a multimodal cycle based on programs and large language models. AutoCreate requires a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate a large quantity of high-quality, diverse data by Large Language Models (LLMs).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We design a novel LLM-based cyclic framework, AutoCreate, for automatic dataset creation... Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: AutoCreate requires a small batch of manually input seeds... Here, the Generator creates initial language/vision data... Within 8 types of conflicts, only SemanticConflict involves extemal data, ImageNet.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For V-L conflicts, the image caption is modified to introduce a conflict. Third, the numerical data is manipulated by changing the maximum value to the minimum value. Third, this phrase is modified to refer to a non-existent object... Second, we substitute the correct label in the questions with some similar but different objects.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: While the generation prompts vary across tasks, the generation process is unified in AutoCreate: generator-decorator-cleaner... the Cleaner removes data that does not meet quality standards. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. The resulting high-quality dataset is then refined to extract new seeds for re-entry into the seed pool.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Finally, human experts have rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset, SCI. Besides that whole dataset, SCI-All, we also introduce two subsets, SCI-Base and SCI-Core, to cater to different needs. The latter subsets are selected manually... Initially, a set of replies generated by LMM on SCI-Core was collected. These replies were then evaluated by both human experts and GPT-4 [32].

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate are calculated to measure the evaluation consistency between humans and LLM. As recorded in Table 2, GPT-4 demonstrates a close alignment to human evaluative standards.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Social Impact Our work on the SCI benchmark, along with the AutoCreate framework and CaP approach, has significant social implications. It provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs’ ability to navigate conflicting instructions... promoting inclusivity in AI research... By improving dissonance detection, our approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Within 8 types of conflicts, only SemanticConflict involves extemal data, ImageNet. This might be due to the difference in their training data.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Limitations To begin with, we only include language-language and vision-language paradigms. More modalities will be included in our SCI benchmark based on our automatic framework, AutoCreate. Besides, no fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. Finally, we do not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce the Self-Contradictory Instructions benchmark to evaluate the capability of LMMs in recognizing conflicting commands... we also introduce two subsets, SCI-Base and SCI-Core... to facilitate qualitative evaluation.
